transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-20 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya T., Ethan P., Lena O. (Redwood) -- Sophie A., Daniel R., Priya N. (Nova)

Summary: quick run through of joint pipeline, two focus deals, technical blockers on private deployment, agreement on next steps.

00:00 Sophie Alvarez: Okay we can start, thanks everyone for joining, weather in SF, just kidding. So this is our co-sell pipeline review with Redwood.
00:18 Maya Thompson: Hey Sophie, hi Daniel, hi Priya, thanks for hosting this. Quick agenda: run through the list of joint accounts, pick top priorities, surface any technical blockers, and decide next steps.
00:34 Daniel Reed: Sounds good. For context we have six accounts we've been pursuing together, two in "late" stage, others in discovery.
00:47 Ethan Park: Hi all, Ethan from Redwood infra, I'll flag anything technical on the two late-stage ones.
00:53 Priya Nair: Quick Q, are we going to talk about product-fit or strictly go-to-market?
01:01 Maya Thompson: Both, but short on product - we just need to confirm there's no hard blocker like VPC peering or on-prem requirements that would slow things down.
01:12 Sophie Alvarez: Great. First deal, "Acme Health" — their legal wants a private deployment and SOC2 plus data residency in us-east-1. They asked about on-prem options.
01:26 Ethan Park: Right, on that one we recommended Redwood Private, which can run in their VPC or on-prem. We may need networking work — VPC peering or private link, and possibly an HSM integration for keys.
01:40 Daniel Reed: What about latency? They care about sub-200ms p95.
01:46 Ethan Park: For typical gen workloads and sequence lengths, our Dedicated pools hit that; Private depends on their infra and GPU mix. Also caching of KV reduces repeated context latency but we should run a quick benchmark.
01:58 Sophie Alvarez: Benchmarks would be great. Can Redwood run a quick perf run against their staging?
02:04 Maya Thompson: Yes, we'll propose a short perf pilot. Ethan, can you own a lightweight benchmark plan?
02:09 Ethan Park: Yep I'll draft one — sample prompts, request distribution, expected metrics, and sample testrig.
02:15 Priya Nair: Also to call out, Acme has strict data retention rules — they want logs removed after 30 days and strong encryption at rest.
02:26 Lena Ortiz: We support customer-managed KMS for keys, and audit logs can be configured; we'll share our security checklist.
02:34 Daniel Reed: Perfect. Next deal is "Greenline Retail" — it's more of a hosted API play, smaller spend but fast time-to-value.
02:44 Sophie Alvarez: For Greenline they prefer hosted initially; the ask was predictable unit cost and some per-route throttling.
02:51 Maya Thompson: Hosted fits, we can offer rate limits and quotas per route; pricing can be aligned with monthly commitments.
03:02 Priya Nair: Question — do we need a separate commercial motion for hosted vs dedicated?
03:07 Maya Thompson: Usually we log hosted as usage-based and Dedicated as reserved capacity; for co-sell we can propose either referral fee or revenue-share depending on Nova's preference. Lena, do we have a partner commercial template?
03:18 Lena Ortiz: Yes, I'll share the co-sell RPM and revenue share options after the call.
03:25 Sophie Alvarez: Awesome. Moving on to technical blockers: for the two late-stage deals Nova infra raised concerns about VPC peering complexity and whether Redwood supports on-prem air-gapped deployments.
03:37 Ethan Park: We do support on-prem and private control plane; air-gap installs need additional ops time. Also, some customers mis-hear KV cache as K-V cash in notes — but it's key-value cache that saves repeated prefixes which helps latency and cost.
03:52 Daniel Reed: Any limits on model variants or quantization when on-prem?
03:58 Ethan Park: We can run quantized variants, but kernel selection and throughput depend on hardware; we'll recommend a small evaluation to pick the right quantization profile. There might be small model-behavior differences to watch for so we run eval prompts.
04:14 Sophie Alvarez: Are there any competitors actively in these accounts?
04:18 Maya Thompson: We've seen Anthropic in a few conversations and GCP/Vertex in infra-led deals; sometimes customers test open-source runtimes too.
04:27 Daniel Reed: Good to know. For Acme specifically they're also talking to a managed infra provider that offers a low-cost hosted endpoint.
04:36 Maya Thompson: That's a common tradeoff — latency and enterprise controls vs lower price. Our angle is predictable performance and security controls which match Acme's checklist.
04:47 Priya Nair: On marketing, Nova wants joint webinars and a reference case if Acme goes live. Do we have co-marketing assets?
04:55 Lena Ortiz: Yes we have a partner deck and a co-marketing playbook, I'll attach links in the follow-up.
05:03 Sophie Alvarez: Great. Back to pipeline — who owns outreach for the top six?
05:10 Daniel Reed: Priya and I will own Greenline and three mid-stage accounts; Sophie we'll own Enterprise pipeline and Redwood can support with SEs.
05:20 Maya Thompson: I'll put together the joint pipeline sheet with stages, ACV estimates, and owners, then share after the call.
05:28 Sophie Alvarez: Perfect. Any unresolved risks?
05:32 Ethan Park: Risk: network topology for Acme could add 2-4 weeks for VPC setup. Risk: quantization/regression on on-prem model variants — we'll need evals.
05:44 Maya Thompson: Mitigations: quick perf pilot for Acme to validate latency, and a model regression test suite for on-prem before go-live.
05:55 Priya Nair: Timeline question — if we start pilot next week, what’s a realistic go-live for Acme?
06:02 Ethan Park: If pilot goes well and infra approvals are quick, 8-12 weeks is realistic for Private with HSM integration; Dedicated or hosted could be faster (2-4 weeks).
06:14 Daniel Reed: Okay that sets expectations.
06:17 Sophie Alvarez: Anything else from Redwood?
06:20 Maya Thompson: We'll share the pipeline sheet, the partner deck, security checklist, and propose a date for the technical deep dive.
06:28 Sophie Alvarez: From Nova — we'll send the updated account list and intro to security lead.
06:32 Maya Thompson: Great, let's recap action items.
06:36 Ethan Park: Quick aside, some transcription errors in our notes sometimes show product names as Redwood "Dedicate" which is fine.
06:44 Maya Thompson: (laughs) noted.
06:46 Recap / Next steps: see action items in follow-up.
06:50 Meeting ends.

Shared artifacts: joint_pipeline_template.xlsx (link in chat), Redwood partner playbook (link), security-checklist.pdf (link).

Notes on transcript quality: medium — a few mis-attributed speaker labels and minor transcription errors (e.g., K-V cash).

End of transcript.
